name: CPU benchmarking and device class
plain: Runs short compute loops to estimate how fast the device is.
meaning: A 50 to 500 ms JS or WebAssembly benchmark, plus worker scaling to test the real core count, ranks a phone or laptop into speed tiers. Used for adaptive quality, bot detection (headless VMs) and as a fingerprint component.

web.api: performance.now() loops; Worker pools; WebAssembly; Atomics

steps: Spawn workers to find parallel scaling

data.metric: Elapsed ms per benchmark, noise 2 to 10%

limits.headline: Can run a short speed test to guess how fast your device is
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, and it takes about 50 to 500 ms
can: Run a short loop and time it
Check how many processor cores really work
Sort your device into a slow, medium or fast tier
Spot bots and change video or game quality to match
cannot: Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A script runs short math loops to estimate how fast and how powerful your device is.
story.for_you: You see nothing, except maybe a tiny delay. The site learns whether your device is slow or fast and may change what it sends you. A fast device may get a richer page.
story.for_makers: Sites use it to serve lighter pages on weak phones. Fraud tools use it to tell a real phone from a busy cloud server. Trackers use it to sort devices into classes.

use_cases.example: A browser game tests your speed once, then picks the right graphics quality.
A streaming site picks the video quality that your device can decode without stutter.
A big shop serves a lighter page with fewer scripts to a slow phone.
A bot detector sees that a batch of visits all run at the same unusual speed, a sign of one server farm.
An ad tech script sorts you into a device class by speed, which helps set ad quality and price.
A web team gathers speed classes from real visitors to learn what it must support.
An online exam site checks the device is fast enough to run the test without freezing.

technical_bounds: Thermal throttling and background tabs distort results

value.abuse: Device tier, VM and bot detection, price discrimination

refs.label: Mowery et al., Heterogeneity in JS performance (W2SP 2011)
